To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) maltreated foster care children have high levels of internalizing and externalizing mental health problems, 2) maltreated foster children have higher levels of internalizing problems than non-maltreated foster children, 3) maltreated foster youth have higher rates of externalizing problems than nonmaltreated foster youth, and 4) maltreatment and placement instability are both associated with mental health problems among foster youth.
